body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Sunday, August 30, 2026, and we’re waking up to a warm morning with temperatures already in the 60s. Overnight, Kern County saw an orchard fire in rural areas, and today’s top story is the community’s return to high school football games with new safety measures in place. Let’s get you caught up.

## The Kern Overnight

Overnight, Kern County crews responded to several incidents across the county. Around 5:59 a.m., firefighters were working an orchard fire in rural Kern County that was reported as actively spreading. Meanwhile, late Friday night, officers were sent to a strong-arm robbery near East California Avenue and Williams Street, where medical aid was also dispatched to the scene. A vehicle crashed into a pole on Niles Street early Saturday morning, prompting a full rescue response. In east Bakersfield, a structure fire was tied to a burnt electrical outlet. Overnight calls also included a welfare check on a woman on oxygen whose husband hadn’t returned after stepping out to take out the trash.

## Today's weather

Today’s weather will see a high near 94° and a low around 68° tonight. It’s currently 68° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and there are no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 64.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that** varsity football returned to Kern County Friday night with new safety measures in place at stadiums across the area. The Liberty Patriots played on their home field against the Menlo-Atherton Bears. While the atmosphere was lively with fans cheering on their teams, safety was clearly top of mind. New security measures included a police presence, additional security at the stadium, and bag searches at the entrance. For some students, the extra precautions helped ease concerns, though the recent tragedy still weighed on many minds.

**KGET 17 tells us that** scores from Week 2 of the high school football season are in. The station has posted the latest results for Bakersfield and Kern County teams, giving fans a look at how their local squads performed over the weekend.

**23ABC also shares the story** of a missing man found dead just hours after his release from jail in Santa Barbara. David Mireles, 53, of Shafter, was reported missing more than five hours after being released from the Main Jail on a misdemeanor DUI charge. His body was discovered in brush near the jail administration building, and while investigators believe he had likely been in that location since shortly after his release, the cause of death remains under investigation.

## Something good

**23ABC highlights** a heartwarming community event: Nova Sorella, a Bakersfield nonprofit, hosted a resource fair Saturday aimed at serving residents who are underserved and often overlooked. The event brought together organizations like Serving Hope and The Open Door Network to connect community members with essential services. Founder PJ Jones organized the fair in honor of her son, Ty Jr. Jones, who was killed by gun violence in January 2017. Saturday marked his birthday, and the fair was meant to bring hope to a community that is underserved, undervalued, and often overlooked.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, several public meetings and events are on the calendar for this week. On Wednesday, September 2, the Police Civil Service Commission will meet at 8:30 a.m., and the Personnel and Processes Committee will convene at 12:00 p.m. On Thursday, September 3, the Planning Commission will hold a meeting at 5:30 p.m.

For entertainment, the Fox Theater has a busy schedule. On Tuesday, September 1, the Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027 will be available. Later in the week, the MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA will take place on Saturday, September 5, along with The Oldies Night: A Night Of Timeless Soul, Doo-Wop, & Classic Oldies. Also on Saturday, Talib Kweli will perform for one night only in Bakersfield. Looking further ahead, JUSTIN WILLMAN: ONE FOR THE AGES TOUR is set for Thursday, September 10, and MAX AMINI LIVE IN BAKERSFIELD! will take the stage on Saturday, September 12.

That’s your Sunday morning brief. Have a great day, Bakersfield.
